title: Frontotemporal dementia
bottleneck: Frontotemporal dementia, the leading cause of dementia under age 60, has no approved disease-modifying treatment and no symptomatic drugs of proven benefit. Its pathology is heterogeneous, involving tau, TDP-43, and FUS, and genetic forms involve progranulin, C9orf72, and MAPT mutations with distinct mechanisms.
why_it_blocks: FTD devastates behavior, language, and executive function in mid-life, striking people in their productive years, yet attracts a fraction of Alzheimer's research funding.
current_state: Progranulin-raising therapies, tau and TDP-43 approaches, and antisense strategies for genetic FTD are in early trials. The field lags Alzheimer's by a decade or more, and the amyloid experience counsels humility about single-pathology strategies. Patient registries and natural-history studies are finally giving trial designers the data needed to run efficient studies. Still, FTD drug development remains years behind Alzheimer's in maturity.

sources.title: Much-hyped Alzheimer's drugs removed amyloid yet brought no meaningful gains over 18 months
